items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: The Three Cohens, with the three of us have a sextet and Avishai my younger brother the trumpet player

ctx.x: I don’t know they probably never thought they would retire. It was like what were you thinking? How did you let the three of us become jazz musicians? They, first of all the parents, I wish everybody had supportive parents like that, that see that their children,

they like something, they are into it and they are dedicated to it and they’re like okay we step out of the way, even if we have worries about how you’re going to survive and what’s going to happen, we’re going to let you do what you’re want to do and support you and help you pay for music lessons and drive you around and drive you around and drive you around, and go to all your youth orchestra concerts and, you know they were there when we were squeaking and they were there when The Three Cohens, with the three…

Oh that’s a happy story. Well I appreciate you taking the time to speak with me and I’m looking forward to hearing you live. When you get to a particular venue that you haven’t been to before does the sort of physical layout, the stage, the auditorium affect your choice of repertoire?
